ts.2: R and C are the grid size; out collects cells whose rain reaches both seas.
ts.3: Try every row sr for the cell where rain starts.
ts.4: Try every column sc of that row as the starting cell.
ts.5: seen stores cells this rain already reached, each as the number r * C + c.
ts.6: The stack holds cells the rain has reached but not yet spread from.
ts.7: nw and se record whether this rain has touched each sea yet.
ts.8: Keep spreading while cells remain and at least one sea is still unreached.
ts.9: Take a cell the rain has reached.
ts.10: A cell on the top or left edge drains into the north-west sea.
ts.11: A cell on the bottom or right edge drains into the south-east sea.
ts.12: Look at the four side neighbours.
ts.13: Skip neighbours outside the grid or already reached.
ts.14: Rain can only flow to a neighbour that is no higher.
ts.15: Mark the neighbour reached so it is never pushed twice.
ts.19: Rain from this cell reached both seas, so it is an answer.
ts.22: Every cell whose rain reaches both seas.

py.4: out collects cells whose rain reaches both seas.
py.5: Try every row sr for the cell where rain starts.
py.6: Try every column sc of that row as the starting cell.
py.7: Fresh search: seen marks reached cells, stack holds cells to spread from.
py.8: Neither sea has been reached yet.
py.9: Keep spreading while cells remain and at least one sea is still unreached.
py.10: Take a cell the rain has reached.
py.11: Touching the top or left edge means the north-west sea is reached.
py.12: Touching the bottom or right edge means the south-east sea is reached.
py.13: Look at the four side neighbours.
py.14: Follow a neighbour inside the grid, not yet reached, and no higher than this cell.
py.15: Mark the neighbour reached so it is never pushed twice.
py.17: Did rain from this cell reach both seas?
py.19: Every cell whose rain reaches both seas.

ts.3: climb(seeds) finds every cell whose rain reaches the seeds, by walking from the sea uphill.
ts.4: seen[r][c] becomes true once rain from that cell is known to reach this sea.
ts.5: Queue of cells to spread from, in breadth-first order.
ts.6: Every edge cell drains into its sea directly; mark each one once and queue it.
ts.7: Process the queue in order; head is the next unprocessed position.
ts.8: Take the next cell known to drain into this sea.
ts.9: Look at the four side neighbours.
ts.10: Skip neighbours outside the grid or already marked.
ts.11: Rain flows here only from a neighbour at least as high; skip lower ones.
ts.12: This neighbour's rain can flow into the current cell and on to the sea.
ts.16: The map of cells that drain into this sea.
ts.18: Seed lists: the edge cells of each sea.
ts.19: The left column seeds the north-west sea, the right column the south-east sea.
ts.20: The top row seeds the north-west sea, the bottom row the south-east sea.
ts.21: Mark which cells drain into each sea.
ts.22: out collects cells that drain into both.
ts.24: Scan every column c of that row.
ts.25: A cell that drains into both seas is an answer.
ts.26: Every cell whose rain reaches both seas.

py.5: climb(seeds) finds every cell whose rain reaches the seeds, by walking from the sea uphill.
py.6: seen[r][c] becomes true once rain from that cell is known to reach this sea.
py.7: Queue of cells to spread from, in breadth-first order.
py.8: Every edge cell in seeds drains into this sea directly.
py.9: Corner cells appear twice among the seeds, so take each only once.
py.10: Mark it as draining into this sea.
py.12: Spread until no cell is left to process.
py.13: Take the next cell known to drain into this sea.
py.14: Look at the four side neighbours.
py.16: Accept a neighbour inside the grid, unmarked, and at least as high: its rain flows here.
py.17: This neighbour drains into the sea through the current cell.
py.19: The map of cells that drain into this sea.
py.21: Cells draining into the north-west sea, seeded from the left column and top row.
py.22: Cells draining into the south-east sea, seeded from the right column and bottom row.
py.23: Return every cell that drains into both seas.
